meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we'll keep this short. Who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before he read it on his phone in the middle of class?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, on what basis was it entered at all?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
Show me the page, with the date on it. A seventeen-year-old asked a vocabulary question cold, with no warning, said "like, being stuck"; that's not exactly a confession. What else do you have, Hale?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

People change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what drafting is for. Still, I'm writing down October 15. Put the outline and the essay side by side and turn the screen so I can read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's procedure 4.4, Hale, the step that should have come before any zero. "If it holds up" according to whom, and who else will be in that room at 8:15? Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged entering the zero before contacting me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require to know who decides whether the rewrite holds up and who else will be present, and I require that this stay private and off Owen's record whatever the outcome. I expect your offer in writing by Friday at 3 PM, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet, and she still wants to know who judges the rewrite and who will be in the room, and wants it kept quiet and off Owen's record.
What moved her: "His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice", because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: "If it holds up", because it was a vague standard with no named judge, so she pressed on it instead of moving.
Try next time: when she asked to see the dated note and the outline side by side, show both on screen before making the offer, and name who will judge the rewrite in the same breath.
